beats.intent: A 1 by 1 square split into a 10 by 10 grid of hundredths
beats.narration: Take a square of side one, cut into a ten by ten grid. Each little square is one hundredth.
beats.code:
stage.title("Multiplying decimals")
s = 0.4
tl = np.array([-5.6, 1.8, 0])
grid = VGroup(*[Square(s, color=GREY_D, stroke_width=1).move_to(tl + np.array([(i + 0.5) * s, -(j + 0.5) * s, 0])) for j in range(10) for i in range(10)])
border = Square(10 * s, color=WHITE).move_to(tl + np.array([5 * s, -5 * s, 0]))
stage.play(FadeIn(grid), Create(border))
stage.add(grid, border)
stage.label(border, "1 × 1", direction=UP)

beats.intent: A strip 0.3 wide shaded across the square in blue
beats.narration: Shade a strip nought point three wide: three columns.
beats.code:
cols = VGroup(*[grid[j * 10 + i] for j in range(10) for i in range(3)])
stage.play(*[c.animate.set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.35) for c in cols])
stage.label(Line(tl, tl + 3 * s * RIGHT), "0.3", direction=UP, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: A strip 0.2 tall shaded across in orange; the overlap is 6 little squares
beats.narration: Now a strip nought point two tall: two rows. Where they overlap is a rectangle nought point three by nought point two: just six little squares.
beats.code:
rows = VGroup(*[grid[j * 10 + i] for j in range(2) for i in range(10)])
stage.play(*[r.animate.set_fill(ORANGE, opacity=0.35) for r in rows])
both = VGroup(*[grid[j * 10 + i] for j in range(2) for i in range(3)])
stage.play(*[b.animate.set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.9) for b in both])
stage.label(Line(tl, tl + 2 * s * DOWN), "0.2", direction=LEFT, color=ORANGE)
stage.label(both, "6 hundredths", direction=RIGHT, color=GREEN)

beats.narration: Six hundredths: nought point nought six. Three times two is six, and tenths times tenths make hundredths.

request: why do co-interior angles between parallel lines add up to 180°?

beats.intent: Two parallel lines crossed by a slanted line
beats.narration: Two parallel lines are crossed by a third line.
beats.code:
stage.title("Co-interior angles")
y1, y2 = 0.8, -1.4
p1 = Line([-6.2, y1, 0], [0.2, y1, 0], color=WHITE)
p2 = Line([-6.2, y2, 0], [0.2, y2, 0], color=WHITE)
d = np.array([np.cos(65 * DEGREES), np.sin(65 * DEGREES), 0])
A = np.array([-3.0, y1, 0])
B = A + (y2 - y1) / d[1] * d
cross = Line(B - 1.0 * d, A + 1.0 * d, color=BLUE)
stage.play(Create(p1), Create(p2), Create(cross))
stage.add(p1, p2, cross)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text(">", font_size=30).move_to([-5.2, y1, 0])), FadeIn(Text(">", font_size=30).move_to([-5.2, y2, 0])))

beats.intent: The angle inside the top line, between the lines on the right, marked 115°
beats.narration: Mark the angle at the top crossing on the inside, between the parallel lines: a hundred and fifteen degrees.
beats.code:
top = Angle(Line(A, A + RIGHT), Line(A, B), radius=0.6, color=YELLOW, other_angle=True)
stage.play(Create(top))
stage.add(top)
stage.label(top, "115°", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The matching inside angle at the bottom crossing marked 65°
beats.narration: On the same side, inside the lines at the bottom crossing, the angle is sixty five degrees.
beats.code:
bot = Angle(Line(B, B + RIGHT), Line(B, A), radius=0.6, color=ORANGE)
stage.play(Create(bot))
stage.add(bot)
stage.label(bot, "65°", direction=RIGHT, color=ORANGE)

beats.narration: These co-interior angles, on the same side and between the parallels, always add to a hundred and eighty: the bottom one matches the angle on the outside of the top crossing, and together those make a straight line.

request: how do you change 3:45 pm into the 24-hour clock?

beats.narration: The clock shows quarter to four, and it's afternoon: three forty five p m.
beats.code:
stage.title("The 24-hour clock")
c = np.array([-4.2, 0.2, 0])
face = Circle(radius=1.6, color=WHITE).move_to(c)
ticks = VGroup(*[Line(c + 1.45 * np.array([np.cos(a), np.sin(a), 0]), c + 1.6 * np.array([np.cos(a), np.sin(a), 0]), color=WHITE) for a in np.arange(0, TAU, TAU / 12)])
ang_h = PI / 2 - (3.75 / 12) * TAU
ang_m = PI / 2 - (45 / 60) * TAU
hour = Line(c, c + 0.9 * np.array([np.cos(ang_h), np.sin(ang_h), 0]), color=YELLOW, stroke_width=7)
minute = Line(c, c + 1.35 * np.array([np.cos(ang_m), np.sin(ang_m), 0]), color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
stage.play(Create(face), Create(ticks), Create(hour), Create(minute))
stage.add(face, ticks, hour, minute)
stage.label(face, "3:45 pm", direction=DOWN, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: A 24-hour line from 0 to 24 with noon at 12 marked
beats.narration: The twenty four hour clock counts on past noon instead of starting again at one.
beats.code:
nl = NumberLine(x_range=[0, 24, 3], length=6, include_numbers=True, font_size=22).move_to([-0.2, -2.3, 0])
stage.play(Create(nl))
stage.add(nl)
noon = Dot(nl.n2p(12), color=BLUE)
stage.play(FadeIn(noon))
stage.add(noon)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("noon", font_size=24, color=BLUE).move_to(nl.n2p(10.6) + 0.55 * UP)))

beats.intent: An arc from noon on to 15:45, three and three-quarter hours later
beats.narration: Three forty five in the afternoon is three hours forty five after noon: twelve plus three, fifteen forty five.
beats.code:
arc = ArcBetweenPoints(nl.n2p(12), nl.n2p(15.75), angle=-PI / 2, color=GREEN)
stage.play(Create(arc))
stage.add(arc)
t = Dot(nl.n2p(15.75), color=GREEN)
stage.play(FadeIn(t))
stage.add(t)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("+ 3 h 45", font_size=26, color=GREEN).move_to(nl.n2p(13.9) + 1.0 * UP)))

beats.narration: For afternoon times, add twelve to the hour.

request: why do the diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles?

beats.intent: A rhombus with all four sides equal, marked with ticks
beats.narration: A rhombus has four equal sides.
beats.code:
stage.title("Diagonals of a rhombus")
c = np.array([-3.2, -0.3, 0])
a, b = 2.4, 1.4
P = [c + a * LEFT, c + b * DOWN, c + a * RIGHT, c + b * UP]
rh = Polygon(*P, color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(rh))
stage.add(rh)
marks = VGroup(*[Line(ORIGIN, 0.2 * UP, color=YELLOW).move_to((P[i] + P[(i + 1) % 4]) / 2).rotate(np.arctan2(*(P[(i + 1) % 4] - P[i])[[1, 0]])) for i in range(4)])
stage.play(Create(marks))
stage.add(marks)

beats.intent: Both diagonals drawn, meeting at the middle M
beats.narration: Draw both diagonals. They meet in the middle.
beats.code:
d1 = Line(P[0], P[2], color=BLUE)
d2 = Line(P[1], P[3], color=ORANGE)
stage.play(Create(d1), Create(d2))
stage.add(d1, d2)
stage.play(FadeIn(Dot(c)), FadeIn(Text("M", font_size=24).next_to(c, DR, buff=0.1)))

beats.intent: The four triangles around M shaded: all congruent, so the four angles at M are equal
beats.narration: The diagonals cut it into four triangles with the same three sides, so they're identical. The four angles at the middle are equal, and four equal angles around a point are ninety degrees each.
beats.code:
tris = VGroup(*[Polygon(c, P[i], P[(i + 1) % 4], color=col, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=0) for i, col in zip(range(4), (BLUE, GREEN, BLUE, GREEN))])
stage.play(FadeIn(tris))
stage.add(tris)
ra = RightAngle(Line(c, P[2]), Line(c, P[3]), length=0.25, color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(ra))
stage.add(ra)

beats.narration: So the diagonals of a rhombus always cross at right angles.
